judgeRationales.scenarioName: Consolidate duplicate public helpers without breaking shipped callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The functional changes are equivalent and satisfy both required outcomes. Both validate the solution tests; run A also explicitly builds Fixture.sln, while B adds a documentation comment, neither creating a meaningful final-result advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a framework and package upgrade dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the required refactoring boundary exactly, refuses the behavior-affecting upgrade, confirms no changes, and routes it correctly. A performs precisely the disallowed work and mischaracterizes it as behavior-preserving.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a new-feature request dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses take the prohibited path of implementing the requested feature and labeling it behavior-preserving, rather than declining and directing the request through the feature workflow. Their rubric compliance is equivalently absent.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract shared discount logic without collapsing distinct inputs
judgeRationales.rationale: The two agents reached the same correct final implementation and reported equivalent successful build/test verification; there is no final-result quality difference.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract subtotal calculation without changing arithmetic
judgeRationales.rationale: Both deliver the requested minimal behavior-preserving refactor. The only implementation difference is that A makes the private helper static while B makes it an instance method; neither affects the requested behavior or rubric compliance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Inline a pass-through wrapper and update callers
judgeRationales.rationale: Both final results satisfy the requested inline refactor with the same focused edits and successful verification; no material quality difference is evidenced.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a shipped nullable contract out of a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs satisfy the misleading requested edit rather than recognizing and preserving the shipped nullable source contract. Their final artifacts and conclusions fail both rubric criteria to the same extent.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep behavior-changing bug fixes out of a behavior-preserving refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B fully follows the refactoring constraint: it safely completes and validates the rename, retains $100 behavior, and clearly defers the incompatible feature change. A makes and masks an invoice behavior change while falsely presenting it as a refactor.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Merge two near-identical types into one parameterized type
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve a serialized name while renaming a C# property
judgeRationales.rationale: The evidence shows materially identical, correct implementations and validation: Tier is the C# API while LoyaltyLevel remains the JSON wire name.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve a shipped wrapper while inlining ordinary callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The runs produce the same minimal, correct refactor and preserve the same compatibility test and public forwarding API. Both have passing multi-target test/build evidence; neither has a material final-result advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a helper used in every target-framework branch
judgeRationales.rationale: Both final results are substantively identical and fully satisfy the rename and label-preservation requirements, with successful solution-level multi-target validation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a member declared by a generated partial source
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents produced the same correct, minimal source changes in the required files and validated them with successful builds and all 17 tests passing for net8.0 and net10.0.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a shipped public method without breaking existing callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The final implementations are substantively equivalent and satisfy all requested compatibility, caller-migration, test, and shipped-surface requirements. Differences such as qualifying Obsolete with System do not affect result quality.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename an internal member used by a friend assembly
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents achieved the requested behavior-preserving rename and friend-assembly migration, with equivalent source-level verification and successful Fixture.sln build/test validation. Run B's initially invalid `--quiet` baseline command was recovered and does not affect the final result.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Choose LSP diagnostics before building
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a language semantic fix in the fallback
judgeRationales.rationale: Both answers are correct and complete. B is marginally stronger because it explicitly preserves ReadLine's nullable EOF behavior and directly emphasizes disposing the wrapper rather than omitting disposal.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely follows the intended stale-discovery recovery sequence and addresses the requested MAUI data-binding workflow. A misdiagnoses the situation and prematurely recommends reinstall/enable actions.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely selects the relevant Blazor specialist and supplies actionable install, restart, and verification steps while respecting the no-implementation constraint. A is non-destructive but substitutes a generic/custom-agent discussion for the requested marketplace-ready specialist workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly selects the relevant named specialist and gives actionable Copilot CLI installation and discovery steps while preserving the requested no-code-change boundary. A diagnoses the issue correctly but does not provide comparably usable marketplace preparation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: B better fulfills the core preparation request through the exact specialist/plugin and complete Copilot CLI restart/discovery workflow. A gives stronger general compatibility detail, but its missing discovery step is a material usability gap.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the available marketplace route to the exact dotnet-webapi specialist and, most importantly, gives verified usable Copilot CLI installation and restart/discovery instructions. A supplies stronger technical upload guardrails but substitutes a custom agent and omits the required post-restart discovery procedure.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: B satisfies every requested preparation detail and is notably stronger on installation verification and post-restart discovery. The core specialist recommendation and non-editing restraint are otherwise equivalent, so the overall quality advantage is slight.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Both reach the correct specialist and safely stop at preparation. B is the better final answer because its Copilot CLI enablement path is concrete and, critically, includes restart plus `/skills` verification, while also making the deployed-evidence versus optimization distinction more direct.

A has a stronger explanation of migration concerns, but its generic community-agent recommendation and manual installation path are less directly aligned with marketplace preparation.

judgeRationales.rationale: Both chose the right specialist and appropriately stopped, but B is materially more usable for the requested Copilot CLI preparation: its installation/discovery workflow is correct and it more concretely addresses migration semantics. judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Both reach the correct specialist and preserve vendor neutrality, but B directly fulfills the central operational requirement with usable marketplace installation, restart, and skill-discovery steps while remaining appropriately scoped to preparation. judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases

judgeRationales.rationale: Both have the same clean .NET-related behavior and the same file-creation violation. A is modestly stronger on the substantive Python response because it offers a more complete pandas-only implementation and chunking guidance, though neither fully guarantees identical output in all edge cases (notably overlapping non-key column names and forced int32 IDs).

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Use the Codex marketplace flow
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the core request with the named maintained marketplace specialist and a usable Codex plugin installation path, while A is largely generic and relies on speculative commands and a made-up example package. Both incompletely discuss migration risks, but B is clearly the substantially more useful and correct result.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Choose LSP diagnostics before building
judgeRationales.rationale: Both deliver a correct, non-editing diagnosis and minimal semantic-preserving repair plan. B is modestly better because its requested LSP action is clearer and does not dilute the diagnostics-first instruction with a build proxy.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a language semantic fix in the fallback
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely diagnoses stale skill discovery and supplies the required restart, listing, and maui-data-binding verification sequence. A does not solve the reported issue and unnecessarily casts doubt on the already successful installation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly names the relevant installable capability and gives a concise, executable Copilot CLI marketplace installation and discovery flow while honoring the no-implementation constraint. A has sound Blazor diagnosis but its Copilot CLI availability guidance is speculative and not operationally usable.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly and accurately answers both requested planning questions with the exact specialist, plugin, install commands, and verification steps, while stopping before implementation. A is vague and lacks actionable installation guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: Both make the correct recommendation and respect the no-edit constraint, but B uniquely fulfills the requested usable post-install restart/discovery workflow and gives the correct Copilot CLI install syntax.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly maps the two requested phases to the actual specialized skills and gives executable marketplace installation and verification instructions, while respecting the no-project-creation boundary. A has the correct high-level phase ordering but substitutes vague custom roles for the requested capability providers.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for a Python request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy all explicit rubric criteria equally. On response quality, A is slightly preferable because its proposed merge preserves the original left-row ordering, whereas B sorts both inputs and therefore changes the ordinary pandas inner-merge output order while claiming the result is unchanged. B also forces an int64 key, which can fail or alter valid string/nullable identifiers, and makes unsupported claims about a sorted merge path. A still has semantic edge cases from converting unmatched categorical values to missing, so the gap is modest.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Use the Codex marketplace flow
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs make the same correct, minimal functional refactor, preserve the shipped APIs, find no production callers requiring migration, and validate successfully. A adds a helpful XML remark, while B separately runs dotnet build in addition to tests; these are minor process/presentation differences with no material final-quality advantage.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline a new-feature request dressed up as a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely follows all three rubric requirements by declining the behavior-changing request and routing it appropriately. A performs the prohibited feature implementation despite passing existing tests.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extract shared discount logic without collapsing distinct inputs
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are behavior-preserving validated refactors, but B has the cleaner and more accurately scoped ApplyTierDiscount helper: it extracts only the tier discount while retaining tax and final rounding in their original separate calculation paths.

judgeRationales.rationale: The final code changes are substantively identical and fully satisfy both requested refactoring and behavior-preservation requirements; both verify the solution successfully.

judgeRationales.rationale: The final code changes satisfy both task requirements equally and are similarly focused. Run B documents a more extensive pre-change check, but that does not make its resulting refactor materially better than Run A's.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a shipped nullable contract out of a refactor
judgeRationales.rationale: B correctly resisted an unsafe request after verifying the API is shipped and clearly explained why no change was appropriate. A implemented precisely the breaking public-contract change the rubric prohibits; passing build/tests does not repair that API compatibility failure.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extend a shipped method with an extra parameter without a binary break
judgeRationales.rationale: Both submissions miss every central compatibility requirement and therefore are substantially incorrect. A is only slightly preferable because it confines the erroneous change to the requested API, whereas B additionally changes ConfigReader and expands parsing behavior beyond the task.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fold a shipped duplicate type into its twin without removing it
judgeRationales.rationale: The implementations are nearly identical and both pass tests while preserving the public compatibility surface. A is marginally closer to the requested caller migration because its repository callers no longer invoke ConfigReader; neither run fully demonstrates the requested public-surface rationale through an Obsolete annotation or explicit baseline explanation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a local-variable rename proportionate inside a shipped library
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents produced the same correct, minimal rename and validated the unchanged behavior with the solution tests. Run 1 additionally searched for remaining occurrences, but this does not create a material final-result quality advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a shipped parameter name stable when asked to rename it
judgeRationales.rationale: B followed the task's safety fallback: it recognized the public compatibility issue, made no unsafe changes, explained why, and validated the solution. A made and baselined a breaking public parameter rename merely because repository callers were positional.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Leave already-shared parsing alone when asked to consolidate it
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents make the same fundamental misdiagnosis despite evidence that ConfigReader already delegates to AppSettingsHelper, perform unnecessary code changes, and report the opposite of the required conclusion. Neither result is meaningfully better.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve a shipped nullability contract
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a member of a partial type that a generated part references
judgeRationales.rationale: The final repository changes are substantively the same: both correctly rename the template and API baseline and pass tests, but both make the same major compatibility error of deleting Redeem instead of retaining it as obsolete forwarding API.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: tie). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely follows the requested stale-discovery recovery flow and identifies the expected MAUI data-binding workflow. A incorrectly treats the issue as an unavailable capability in its own environment and does not help refresh discovery.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the requested specialist selection and provides actionable Copilot CLI preparation and verification steps while respecting the no-implementation constraint. A misses the available specialist and does not provide usable CLI installation instructions.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly and concisely fulfills all requested elements with a named specialist, actionable Copilot CLI setup/discovery instructions, and no utility code. A fails the core specialist and installation requests.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: A's recommendation and installation command are directly grounded in the maintained `github/awesome-copilot` `dotnet-upgrade` skill discovered during its run. B provides more explicit post-restart wording but centers on an unsubstantiated specialist and installation route, making its core answer unreliable. A's only meaningful omission is explicit post-restart discovery guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Both correctly select the specialist and avoid changing the fixture. B is better because it directly addresses fixture isolation and, most importantly, gives a complete install, restart, and discovery path; that is a meaningful but bounded improvement over A.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: B is grounded in the actual ASP.NET Core project and the exact marketplace specialist, with actionable install, restart, and discovery instructions. A gives technically sensible upload guidance but recommends a custom agent and weaker availability steps.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses fulfill the task well and accurately. B is modestly stronger because its explanation more directly and completely ties the specialist to the requested round-trip reduction while preserving the returned shape.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Stay dormant for a Python request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy the rubric cleanly, but A is modestly more precise and polished, while B makes an unsupported indexed/sorted-merge claim and leaves dead code.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Use the Codex marketplace flow
judgeRationales.rationale: A is the more complete and operationally useful marketplace-preparation answer, particularly on the skill's scope and Codex discovery. B is better at briefly identifying an isolation/parameterized-case preservation concern, but both inadequately explain the full set of pre-migration risks.

judgeRationales.rationale: Response B provides a cleaner, more direct path to using an existing marketplace specialist. It identifies maui-data-binding from the dotnet-maui plugin with marketplace installation steps and a verification method, which aligns better with how Copilot CLI marketplace functionality works. judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy the .NET-dormancy and no-file-change requirements. B is better at mentioning a fixture-isolation risk, but its risk discussion remains incomplete and does not outweigh A's stronger installation guidance.

Response B used slightly more robust shell scripting practices (set -o pipefail, structured variable output) and activated an msbuild skill, though the skill didn't add practical value to the core task. Both responses are functionally equivalent in meeting all three rubric criteria."

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Keep a language semantic fix in the fallback
judgeRationales.rationale: Both answers correctly solve the ownership issue in their main snippets, but A undermines its answer with an alternative that leaks the disposable StreamReader. B is consistently safe and minimal.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Recover an installed but undiscovered plugin
judgeRationales.rationale: B is substantially closer to the requested MAUI data-binding discovery outcome: it recognizes the plugin and names the expected `maui-data-binding` skill, and includes reload then listing. However, it unnecessarily directs installation/reinstallation before that basic discovery recovery. A misdiagnoses the already-installed skill as absent and diverts to unrelated MAUI workload/cloud-agent setup.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly fulfills all requested preparation steps with the exact specialist/skill and actionable Copilot CLI installation, restart, and verification instructions. A is directionally correct about Blazor ownership but misses the central marketplace/CLI availability request.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: B fulfills the task precisely with an evidence-based MAUI specialist selection, correct Copilot CLI acquisition commands, discovery verification, and no code change. A is generic and does not provide usable marketplace installation steps.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers both the owning specialist and how to install/discover it in Copilot CLI, with concrete commands and no generated utility. A is based on an unrelated unavailable dynamic-workflows tool and fails the central requested workflow and installation guidance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: A is more actionable overall because it gives a concrete maintained source and executable Copilot CLI setup/verification steps, while B's named specialist is more direct but its installation guidance is too vague to use. Both remain incomplete on explicit restart and detailed compatibility scope.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: B is grounded in the detected ASP.NET Core project and directly fulfills the request for a specialist with actionable Copilot CLI installation and discovery steps. A has sound generic upload guidance but misses the concrete app-specific specialist and CLI setup.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Add a new public method that must be correct on every target framework
judgeRationales.rationale: Both implementations satisfy all requested functional, packaging-surface, compatibility, and test requirements. Response B is more explicit in its final compatibility narrative and lists per-TFM commands, but Response A's recorded full solution test likewise demonstrably exercised both frameworks, so this is not a material final-result quality difference.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Add behavior to a shipped public member without breaking the contract
judgeRationales.rationale: B delivers the required overload-based API evolution and retains the shipped signature, with a minor redundant Unshipped API entry. A's working feature/test uses an optional parameter and rewrites the shipped API, violating the central compatibility and API-baseline requirements.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Extend a shipped method with an extra parameter without a binary break
judgeRationales.rationale: Both fail the essential API-shape and API-baseline requirements. B is only marginally preferable: it adds a genuine de-DE culture parsing test using AllowThousands and avoids A's explicit misleading compatibility assertion; it still does not deliver the required compatible overload solution.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Fold a shipped duplicate type into its twin without removing it
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Leave already-shared parsing alone when asked to consolidate it
judgeRationales.rationale: Both agents made essentially equivalent, behavior-preserving but unnecessary refactors and reported the same incorrect conclusion. Neither satisfies any of the task's intended rubric outcomes.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Preserve a shipped nullability contract
judgeRationales.rationale: Both miss the task's central shipped-contract safeguard by rewriting the baseline, so neither is a good result. B is modestly better because its AllowNull annotation materially attempts to retain source compatibility for existing null callers, whereas A knowingly leaves them subject to nullable diagnostics.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a member of a partial type that a generated part references
judgeRationales.rationale: B implements the required compatibility-preserving API evolution, updates the generator input, records the additive surface correctly, and validates both target frameworks. A performs a breaking rename (and an unnecessary default-helper rename), failing the central retained obsolete-forwarder requirement.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a public method in a private single-target app without compatibility ceremony
judgeRationales.rationale: The trajectories and final outcomes are substantively identical: both implement the requested direct rename, update the caller, preserve behavior, and validate with a clean build.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a vague public method without breaking existing callers
judgeRationales.rationale: The implementations are substantively the same: each passes the platform tests but makes the same two public-API compatibility/baseline mistakes. Neither has a meaningful quality advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename an internal member used by a friend assembly
judgeRationales.rationale: The final code changes are substantively identical: both complete the local rename and test update but miss the required compatibility handling for the out-of-repository Billing.Plugins friend assembly.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Review a green pull request for consumer-breaking changes
judgeRationales.rationale: Both give the correct do-not-merge verdict and identify the three substantive consumer breaks without false positives. B is more complete on the compatibility-baseline concealment and the edited NET8 test, and explicitly addresses the non-breaks and unchanged repository.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a Blazor component request
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the available documented specialist mapping and gives actionable Copilot CLI marketplace installation and discovery steps while making no implementation changes. A's answer is based on an incorrect conclusion that no relevant specialist exists and substitutes an unnecessary custom agent.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a MAUI binding defect
judgeRationales.rationale: B precisely selects the demonstrated MAUI binding skill and provides the requested Copilot CLI marketplace installation and discovery flow without modifying code. A gives a plausible diagnosis but misses the existing specialist and replaces the requested marketplace path with an unnecessary custom-agent proposal.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a file based CSharp request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the ownership question with the correct specialized plugin and gives concise, actionable installation and verification steps while respecting the request not to write the utility. A is based on the erroneous premise that no relevant capability exists, so its custom-agent workaround does not satisfy the intended workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a framework upgrade
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route a test framework migration
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are correct, concise, and satisfy the requested preparation-only scope. A is modestly stronger because it verifies and reports the project's concrete NUnit setup and fixture-state concern, making the guidance more actionable for this particular migration.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an ASP.NET Core endpoint request
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy the preparation-only request and recognize the web stack, but B delivers the notably more actionable Copilot CLI acquisition and discovery workflow and recommends a concrete available specialist. A's superior project-specific detail does not offset its vague custom-agent setup.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an EF Core query optimization
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are accurate, concise, and fully satisfy the requested preparation-only workflow. A has a marginally stronger explanation of the repeated-query mechanism and relevant capability, without crossing into implementation.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route an MSBuild binlog failure
judgeRationales.rationale: A gives the precise MSBuild failure and minimal existence-based repair while carefully separating what the binlog proves from what it cannot establish, including file content and repository layout. B reaches the main filename but overstates certainty about CI configuration and unspecified schema content. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Route runtime performance evidence
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses are correct, concise, and satisfy every requested operational boundary. A is marginally stronger because it establishes the specialist's maintained/runtime-diagnostics fit and exclusions more concretely, without crossing into collection or diagnosis.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Sequence distinct template and component phases
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Use the Codex marketplace flow
judgeRationales.rationale: Both are largely correct and stop short of migration. judgeRationales.scenarioName: Rename a shipped public method without breaking existing callers
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B is slightly better overall. While both solutions achieve the core objectives of migrating callers and preserving backward compatibility, Response B implements the deprecation pattern more correctly and professionally. The key advantages are: (1) it properly marks the old method with [Obsolete] attribute, which is the standard .NET practice for deprecated APIs, making it discoverable to IDEs and developers; (2) it includes pragma warning directives in the legacy test, explicitly documenting and suppressing the obsolete warning to show intentional use of the deprecated API; and (3) these professional touches align better with best practices for API versioning in .NET. Both solutions successfully preserve PublicAPI.Shipped.txt and migrate callers appropriately, but Response B demonstrates a more mature approach to API deprecation."

Since the rubric focuses on the quality of the final result and not operational efficiency, and both produced identical correct outcomes, they are equivalent."
